title: Correct Decoding of the Scanned Input
statement: Let $\Gamma,S,S'$ be types, let $k$ be a natural number, let $x$ be a finite word over $\Gamma$, and let $c$ be a configuration with $k$ work tapes on input $x$. Let $d$ be a one-work-tape configuration over the enlarged sweep alphabet on the symbol-wise encoded input, and suppose its input-head position equals the transported position of the input head of $c$. Then decoding the symbol scanned by $d$ gives exactly the symbol scanned by $c$.
hypotheses_covered: $c$ is a configuration with $k$ work tapes on input $x$
$d$ is a configuration over the enlarged sweep alphabet on the encoded input
The input-head position of $d$ equals the transported input-head position of $c$
replaced:
Let $c$ be a configuration of a $k$-work-tape machine on input $x$, and let $d$ be a
configuration of any machine over the enlarged sweep alphabet on the symbol-wise encoded
input whose input head is at the transported position of $c$'s input head. Then decoding
the input symbol scanned by $d$ yields exactly the input symbol scanned by $c$.
